verdicts.reasoning: READ: onCommitted appends `{ version, content: "", origin: "edit" }` and bumps currentVersion via onArtifactUpdated. chat-view.tsx:1254-1262 stores that object as-is in chat.artifacts. The effect at canvas-panel.tsx:313-315 moves selectedVersion to the new version. The editor is keyed on selectedVersion (canvas-panel.tsx:1237), and versionContent resolves to "" because `??` does not fall back on an empty string (369-370). use-design-document.ts:170-188 re-parses on the new initialContent. parseStoredDesignDocument("") throws 'Design document is not valid JSON' (migrations.ts:91-97), and design-editor.tsx:520-534 then shows the error. The trigger is real. Chat-generated designs are stored with origin 'generated' (artifacts-store.ts:59,86), and so are hand-started designs (api/design/route.ts ~88). allocatesCheckpoint returns true when latest.origin !== 'edit' (operations.ts:535), and it also returns true for any edit after 30 s. httpTransport reports the new currentVersion, which fires the early-return guard only for a fold. Two small corrections. First, the on-screen text is 'This design can't be opened' with 'Design document is not valid JSON', not 'could not be read'. Second, the placeholder also leaks elsewhere: while it is current, the Code tab, Copy, Download (displayedContent) and the History diff all read the in-session checkpoint as empty. I searched for a mitigation and found none. A later model turn does replace the artifact wholesale through mergeArtifacts (use-chat.ts:344-352), which is why a restore of the "" row is not reachable. The bug hits every door that opens a design in the Canvas: /artifacts, search, Outputs and the inline card.

READ: postSchema is `content: z.string().max(200_000)` with no type check. The POST appends a version for any artifact type, including DESIGN, and never goes through commitTransaction or schema validation. That contradicts store.ts:9-11. The Mac (DesktopDesignScreen.swift:577-581 → NativeArtifactStore.saveArtifact, NativeArtifactStore.swift:321-336) and iOS (JunoMobileWorkspaceViews.swift:2067 and the Save button in designDraftControls ~2270-2273) do write whole design bodies through this route. So the product context calling iPhone design 'read-only' is out of date: iPhone edits and saves. The native clients do send baseVersion, and the web Canvas's Code tab is read-only for designs (canvas-panel.tsx:1353-1355). Severity is lowered because I found no first-party path that writes a body the web cannot parse. Native bodies are re-encoded from Swift-decoded documents (DesktopArtifactCanvas.swift:1066-1080), and zod defaults fill any key they lack. The owner-only check means an arbitrary body can only corrupt the caller's own design. The real present-day harm is that this route is the conduit for history-concepts-3's field stripping and for the revision rewind described in missed-1.

READ: DesignDocumentCodec.decode gates only on `version <= DesignSchema.version` and then decodes with Codable, which drops unknown keys (DesignDocumentCodec.swift:43-57). DesignDocument.swift:12-20 calls the contract the referee, but nothing reads contracts/design/design-document.v1.schema.json. The only references are the generator script and comments. No workflow runs `design:contract:check` (package.json:82; the only design gate in .github/workflows is release-ios.yml:76 for the editor bundle). cornerSmoothing was added in c69ee98e (2026-08-15) as `cornerSmoothingSchema.default(0)` (schema.ts:332). DESIGN_SCHEMA_VERSION stays 1 (types.ts:24), and DesignSchema.version stays 1 (DesignDocument.swift:23). Swift has no cornerSmoothing, and DesignDocument.swift was last changed in 390ade91 on 08-06. The round-trip fixture sign-in.juno.design.json was also last changed 08-06 and has zero cornerSmoothing keys. On the Mac the document is decoded to Swift before the editor opens it, and each accepted transaction comes back as a Swift DesignDocument that is re-encoded (DesktopDesignEditorHost.swift:132-163; DesktopArtifactCanvas.swift:1066-1080). A Mac save therefore stores a body with no cornerSmoothing, the web parses it back as 0, and the loss is silent. Severity is lowered to medium because today the loss is one visual property. The governance gap itself is systemic.

RAN: `node scripts/build-design-editor.mjs --check` (a read-only branch at build-design-editor.mjs:190-203) printed 'bundle is stale (expected 1.0.0+9cc1cfa8d4fe)' and exited 1. The shipped index.html stamps 1.0.0+2b86e5baaf9d, and the bundle directory was last changed in 2fa09d35 (2026-09-17). `git log 2fa09d35..HEAD` over src/lib/design, src/components/design and src/components/ui/icon-swap.tsx (the hashed sources) lists exactly 11 commits, and `0a3087fe..HEAD` over the same paths is empty. So Mac 1.6.0's tree carried the stale bundle; that it shipped this bundle is inferred. The test at design-host-bridge.test.ts:77-98 is titled '…and current' but asserts only the script tag, CSP and remote origins, never the version hash. Only release-ios.yml:76 runs design:editor:check. I found no editor build or check step in release-macos.yml, native.yml or any .sh/.mjs release script.

READ: getSharedArtifactSnapshot picks the newest version with `createdAt <= snapshotAt` (share.ts:244-256) and promises that edits stay private (share.ts:10-16). rewriteVersion updates only `content` of the newest row, and createdAt is never touched (store.ts:179-197). The fold decision uses `Date.now() - latest.createdAt` (store.ts:122-125) against CHECKPOINT_WINDOW_MS = 30_000 (operations.ts:511). The window runs from when the row was created, not from the last edit. Edits made after a share, while that row is under 30 s old, therefore change what the public link renders. The window is narrow, so low is right.

missed.title: Restoring a design version through the generic artifact route rewinds the document's `revision`, the design protocol's only concurrency token
missed.evidence: READ: Canvas Restore posts the old version's body verbatim through POST /api/artifacts/[id] (canvas-panel.tsx:442-446 → appendVersion 420-438; route.ts:39-89 stores it unchanged). Mac and iOS restoreArtifact do the same (NativeArtifactStore.swift:339-355). The stored DesignDocument.revision therefore goes back to the old version's value. Transactions are accepted when `transaction.baseRevision === doc.revision` (operations.ts:359), and each one sets revision = doc.revision + 1 (operations.ts:382). After a restore, revision numbers are minted again for different contents. INFERRED: this is an ABA window.
missed.failure_scenario: A design is at revision 8. A second tab or the Mac has an editor acked at revision 6 on the old line. Someone restores v2 (revision 5) in the chat Canvas, and one more edit takes the store to a new revision 6. The stale editor's next transaction carries baseRevision 6 and is accepted against a different document. Its operations then apply to content its author never saw, with no conflict reported.

missed.title: A hand-started blank design is recorded as 'Generated' output
missed.evidence: READ: POST /api/design creates the starter frame with `versions: { create: { version: 1, content: ..., origin: "generated" } }` (route.ts ~81-89). The Canvas history labels origin 'generated' as 'Generated' (canvas-panel.tsx:139-149). The same origin makes the user's first edit always allocate a new checkpoint (operations.ts:535), which feeds history-concepts-1 when the design is opened from /artifacts.
missed.failure_scenario: A user starts a blank design from /design or /artifacts and opens its history in the chat Canvas. v1, an empty frame the user created, is labelled 'Generated', as if Juno made it.
